description: Patch releases of PrivateBin are NOT automerged here, and the reason is PrivateBin's own database upgrade path. When `privatebin_config_model` is `mysql`, `postgres` or `sqlite`, PrivateBin compares the VERSION row it keeps in its `privatebin_config` table against the version of the code that just started, and runs `_upgradeDatabase()` unattended if the code is newer (lib/Data/Database.php). Those migrations are destructive and one-way: `ALTER TABLE paste DROP COLUMN postdate`, `DROP COLUMN opendiscussion`, `DROP COLUMN burnafterreading`, `DROP COLUMN attachment`, `DROP COLUMN attachmentname`, `ALTER TABLE comment DROP COLUMN nickname`. There is no downgrade, so a bad automerge cannot be undone by pinning the previous tag.

That would still be acceptable if migrations were a minor/major-only affair, the way listmonk's are. They are not. The gates are `version_compare($oldversion, ...)` against '0.21', '1.3', '1.7.1' and '1.7.8', and the '1.7.1' one was introduced by the PATCH release 1.7.4: at 1.7.3 lib/Data/Database.php still upgraded through a `switch ($oldversion)` with no such block, and at 1.7.4 it had been rewritten to the version_compare form with the `postdate` column drop in it. Anyone who restarted a 1.7.1 container onto the 1.7.4 image lost a column to a patch bump. Nothing stops 2.0.x from adding a `<= '2.0.6'` block the same way.

A fresh-install test cannot see any of this. The Molecule scenarios create the schema from scratch at the new version, so `_upgradeDatabase()` never runs in CI no matter how thorough the run is - which is exactly the shape of risk the fleet declines automerge for. Minor, major and patch bumps therefore all arrive as pull requests a human looks at.

What CI does cover is everything short of that, so a reviewed bump is a cheap one to approve: the `default`, `mariadb` and `postgres` scenarios each post a paste over PrivateBin's JSON API and read it back, look the row up in the storage backend they claim to be testing, assert the running PrivateBin stamps `privatebin_version` onto the assets it serves, and assert the instance name and paste size limit that only a config.php rendered by this role could have produced.

`versioning=semver` on the annotation in defaults/main.yml is what keeps the noise out of this. privatebin/nginx-fpm-alpine publishes each release twice - `2.0.6` and `2.0.6-alpine3.24` - plus `latest`, `stable`, `edge` and `nightly`. Strict semver reads the flavoured tags as prereleases and skips them as unstable, and the four floating tags are not versions at all, leaving only the plain `2.0.6` line of tags.

`privatebin_version_alpine` is deliberately not tracked by Renovate. It selects the git tag the self-build scenario clones (`<version>-alpine<alpine version>`), and PrivateBin/docker-nginx-fpm-alpine publishes nothing but flavoured tags there, so its correct value is 'whichever Alpine upstream tagged this release against' - not 'the newest Alpine'. Tracking Alpine's own releases would propose 3.25 before upstream had tagged anything against it and break self-building. The bump-gated `default-selfbuild` CI job is the safety net instead: it runs on any branch that changes a version in defaults/main.yml and fails if the resulting git tag does not exist upstream.
